reviewed_checks: Python syntax compilation passed for the exact reviewed script.
The report compares ALS with FM150 and GBT120 only on the common cap10, h>0, W_DIRECT user and movie axis.
The report keeps ALS absent from ALL, C, NATURAL_ZERO, and full-catalog quality tables where ALS has no direct score.
FM and GBT are identified as three-seed user-metric means rather than prediction ensembles, while ALS is identified as an older single-fit reference with its original calibrator.

Metric denominators are derived and asserted consistently: W_DIRECT MSE, MAE, and NDCG@1 use 122 users; NDCG@2 and Top2 measures use 109; NDCG@4 uses 96; NDCG@6 uses 86; ALL errors use 124 and ALL Top2 measures use 117.
ALS-relative MSE, MAE, NDCG, Top2 rating, good-rating, and low-rating deltas are calculated from the sealed per-user outputs; the displayed headline values match those calculations.
Catalog support counts are fixed and checked as 85,517 total, 45,074 W_DIRECT, 10,952 C, and 29,491 NATURAL_ZERO, with 40,443 movies outside ALS item-factor support.
The six FM and GBT catalog score sets are checked across 1,080 user-model rows and require finite_scores to equal candidates before claiming computational coverage.
The final344 input lock and selection, calibration, evaluation, and catalog seals are verified before result extraction.
The combination340 fit seal is linked to its input lock, pins the ALS model seal, and the ALS model seal pins every model child read for support analysis.
The script requires the preserved NO_CLEAR_WINNER_OR_TRADEOFF result and service_adoption false before emitting a conditional GBT implementation candidate.

The report explicitly separates statistical decision, conditional implementation priority, and service adoption, so GBT120 is not presented as a statistically proven winner or an adopted production model.
The figure separates common W_DIRECT quality from catalog support, starts value axes at zero, labels directionality, and annotates ALS-relative differences and the ALS support ceiling.
All logical source, count, direction, exposure, and timing checks occur before the first persistent output write.
Existing report, figure, CSV, and manifest paths are protected from overwrite, and the manifest pins the exact script, review record, sources, and generated outputs.
limitations: This is a static pre-execution review. No report, CSV, or figure was generated or visually inspected in this review; generated artifacts still require independent numerical and visual review.

ALS is an older single-fit descriptive reference, whereas FM150 and GBT120 are three-seed metric means. No preregistered ALS-versus-model confidence interval exists, so ALS-relative differences remain descriptive.
The evidence is DEVELOPMENT_ONLY on reused MovieLens users and does not establish 2026 Korean-user satisfaction or online service performance.
Finite full-catalog scores establish computational coverage, not recommendation quality for UNKNOWN or otherwise unevaluated movies.

GBT120 is only a conditional implementation-priority candidate under the stated full-catalog, Top2, and low-rating-risk priorities; the statistical winner and service-adoption decisions remain unresolved and deferred.

The four write-once outputs are not committed as one atomic filesystem transaction. An exceptional I/O failure after the first write would require preserving and auditing the partial outputs before a deliberate rerun.
